name: Driver
definition: A person who competes in Formula 1 race events. The workload refers to this concept as driver, player or racer.
scope: Driver identity, personal attributes and career-spanning analysis

name: Constructor
definition: A team or manufacturer that enters cars in Formula 1 race events.
scope: Team identity, team attributes and team-level aggregation

name: Race event
definition: A single Grand Prix event held in one season at one circuit. A race event is one round of a championship year.
scope: Race-level analysis; identified by race identifier or by event name together with season

name: Season
definition: A championship year to which race events belong.
scope: Season-level and cross-season analysis

name: Circuit
definition: A physical motorsport venue at which race events are held.
scope: Venue identity, geography and venue-level race counting

name: Race result entry
definition: The classification record of one driver, driving one constructor's car, in one race event. It carries the finishing position, time, points and status of that participation.
scope: Per race per driver outcome analysis

name: Qualifying entry
definition: The record of one driver's participation in the qualifying session of one race event, holding the best lap of each qualifying segment and the resulting qualifying order.
scope: Qualifying analysis, available only for race events from 1994 onward

name: Pit stop
definition: A single pit stop made by one driver during one race, identified by the stop sequence number within that race.
scope: Pit stop analysis, available only for recent race events

name: Driver standing
definition: A driver's cumulative championship position and points total after a given race event within a season.
scope: Cumulative championship analysis over drivers

name: Constructor standing
definition: A constructor's cumulative championship position and points total after a given race event within a season.
scope: Cumulative championship analysis over constructors

name: Driver full name
definition: The complete personal name of a driver, formed by combining the driver's given name and family name. Workload questions refer to a driver by this full name.
scope: Identifying a driver in natural-language questions

name: Race finish
definition: The property of a driver having completed and been classified at the end of a race, as opposed to retiring or otherwise not finishing.
scope: Filtering to drivers who completed a race; also used in negated form for drivers who did not finish

name: Race winner
definition: The driver classified first in a race event. Workload questions may call this driver the champion of that Grand Prix.
scope: Identifying the first-placed driver of a single race

name: Race time value
definition: The time recorded for a driver's race outcome. The same column carries two different quantities: the absolute elapsed race duration for the winner, and a gap relative to the winner for the other classified finishers.
scope: Interpreting, comparing and combining recorded race times

name: Circuit coordinates
definition: The geographic position of a circuit expressed as a latitude and longitude pair in decimal degrees.
scope: Locating a circuit or the venue of a race event

name: Introduction website
definition: A descriptive reference page associated with a driver or a constructor.
scope: Retrieving the profile or introduction link of a driver or constructor

name: Qualifying period
definition: One of the timed segments of a qualifying session in which drivers set a best lap; a driver advances to the next segment only by being fast enough in the current one.
scope: Qualifying segment analysis and elimination reasoning

name: Fastest lap
definition: The quickest lap recorded in a race, together with the rank of a given driver's quickest lap within that race.
scope: Fastest lap analysis, available only for the modern era of the data

name: Driver identifier
definition: The numeric surrogate key that uniquely identifies a driver.
scope: Joining driver-scoped records across tables

name: Driver reference name
definition: A short human-readable reference string identifying a driver, distinct from the numeric key and from the driver's full name.
scope: Addressing a driver by reference name in questions and output

name: Nationality
definition: The country affiliation recorded for a driver or a constructor, expressed as a demonym rather than as a country name.
scope: Filtering drivers or constructors by affiliation such as British or German

name: Date of birth
definition: The calendar date on which a driver was born, which determines the driver's age relative to a race date.
scope: Age and birth-period reasoning over drivers

name: Race identifier
definition: The numeric surrogate key that uniquely identifies a single race event. Workload questions express it as a race number.
scope: Addressing one specific race event regardless of its name or season

name: Race name
definition: The title of a Grand Prix event, such as Canadian Grand Prix. The title recurs across seasons and does not identify a single event by itself.
scope: Naming a Grand Prix event; must be combined with a season or replaced by a race identifier to select one event

name: Race date
definition: The calendar date on which a race event was held.
scope: Chronological ordering, earliest-event and month-based race analysis

name: Circuit location
definition: The town or locality in which a circuit is situated.
scope: Describing where a circuit is, at a finer grain than its country

name: Circuit country
definition: The country in which a circuit is located, expressed as a country name.
scope: Selecting circuits by country and counting race events held within a country

name: Finishing position
definition: The order in which a driver is classified at the end of a race, or the ordering index that ranks all entrants of a race including those that were not classified.
scope: Ranking drivers within a race result; the workload phrase track number denotes this finishing order

name: Grid position
definition: The starting slot assigned to a driver on the starting grid before the race.
scope: Starting-order analysis, distinct from the finishing order

name: Qualifying position
definition: The order resulting from the qualifying session of a race, which determines the starting grid.
scope: Qualifying order analysis

name: Race status
definition: The coded outcome of a driver's race entry, distinguishing a classified finish from disqualification, lapped classification and the many retirement causes.
scope: Describing why and how a driver's race ended

name: Accident
definition: A race outcome in which the driver's entry ended because of an accident. It is one specific value of the race status vocabulary, distinct from collision and from fatal accident.
scope: Counting or filtering accidents as a race outcome

name: Points
definition: Championship points awarded to a driver or constructor for a race, or accumulated by a driver or constructor over a season. Points exist at both per-race and cumulative grains.
scope: Scoring, ranking by score and finding zero-score or maximum-score entries

name: Lap time
definition: The elapsed time taken by one driver to complete one lap of a race.
scope: Lap-level pace analysis, available only for race events from 1996 onward

name: Fastest lap speed
definition: The speed recorded on a driver's fastest lap of a race.
scope: Speed-based comparison of drivers, available only for the modern era

name: Pit stop duration
definition: The elapsed stationary time of a single pit stop made by a driver in a race.
scope: Pit stop timing, available only for recent race events

name: Average pit stop duration
definition: The mean of a driver's individual pit stop durations, normally taken over a race or over a driver's whole record.
scope: Comparing drivers by typical pit stop speed
